common_name: Ace of Hearts Redbud (Compact Round-Leaf Dwarf Redbud)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped trees in late winter, spring, or fall in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Ace of Hearts stays notably smaller and denser than standard redbud, making it a good fit for small yards and foundation plantings.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, siting it where its small mature size and dense canopy can be appreciated up close. Ace of Hearts is a dwarf, compact selection of eastern redbud, reaching roughly half the size of the species, with small, glossy, heart-shaped leaves packed tightly along the branches and a rounded, tidy habit that needs little pruning to stay in bounds. Like other redbuds it flowers on bare wood in early spring with a dense flush of small rosy-pink pea-like blooms before the leaves emerge, followed by clean, deep-green summer foliage that holds its glossy texture better in heat than the species form. Its small stature makes it well suited to foundation plantings, patios, and smaller residential landscapes where a full-sized redbud would quickly outgrow the space.

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped trees in late winter, spring, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; like other Texas-variety redbuds, Texas White tolerates heat, drought, and alkaline soils notably better than standard eastern redbud.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to alkaline soil in full sun; Texas White is a white-flowered selection of the Texas botanical variety of eastern redbud, combining the glossy, leathery, heat-tolerant foliage and superior drought resistance of Texas redbud with pure white spring flowers instead of the typical magenta-pink. The crisp white bloom against bare branches in late winter to early spring provides a striking contrast to pink- and purple-flowered redbuds nearby, and the same waxy, dark green summer leaves resist the leaf scorch and drop that afflicts standard eastern redbud in Gulf Coast heat. Like other Texas redbud selections it is well adapted to alkaline, clay, and rocky soils and needs little supplemental water once established, making it a reliable, low-maintenance small flowering tree for the Gulf South.

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped trees in late winter, spring, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; Traveller is grafted at a chosen height, since the weeping growth habit does not naturally form a trunk, and needs staking while young until the graft union is strong.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun, choosing a prominent spot where the cascading, ground-sweeping branches can be fully appreciated. Traveller is a weeping selection of Texas redbud discovered as a chance seedling in Texas, grafted onto an upright trunk to create a small, umbrella-like specimen tree whose branches drape strongly downward, often trailing along the ground if left unpruned. It carries the same glossy, heat-tolerant leaves and superior drought and alkaline-soil tolerance as other Texas redbud selections, along with a dense flush of pink-magenta flowers on bare weeping branches in early spring. Because the graft union determines the tree's ultimate height and the weeping habit has no natural upright growth, stake young trees to develop a strong trunk and prune only to remove crossing or damaged branches, leaving the cascading form largely undisturbed.
